scales.effort: 1 tiny, 2 small, 3 medium, 4 large, 5 very large. Derived from reference lines, then adjusted where the reference is bloated or unusually dense.
scales.risk: 1 routine, 2 some unknowns, 3 exactness or fidelity matters, 4 hard to verify or heavily unknown, 5 could invalidate the plan.
scales.difficulty: effort x risk. Bands: 1-4 green, 5-9 yellow, 10-14 orange, 15-25 red.
scales.progress: ported = the code exists and compiles. verified = it is checked against the oracle or a real corpus. Ported without verified is not done.

modules.name: Fixed-point math
modules.why: Determinism rests on it. A subtle rounding difference diverges every replay, and the symptom appears far from the cause.

modules.name: Seeded RNG
modules.why: Must be reproducible across platforms and stable forever: changing the sequence invalidates every stored replay.

modules.name: Ids, handles, pooling
modules.why: Shapes the allocation behaviour of everything above it, so getting it wrong is expensive to undo.

modules.name: Invariant guards
modules.why: Cheap, and it is what keeps the other invariants real. Each guard must be seen to fail.

modules.name: Clean-room checking
modules.why: Protects the premise of the whole project, and a clean result proves less than people assume.

modules.name: Oracle harness
modules.why: Every fidelity claim in phase 4 depends on it. Partly exists already as the playtest harness.

modules.name: Archive container
modules.why: Format is trivial and already decoded once: 253 archives, 63,117 entries, zero failures.

modules.name: Textures
modules.why: 27,370 files, 3.76 GB. Volume rather than subtlety, but a wrong decode is silent.

modules.name: Meshes and CLOD
modules.why: 3,607 meshes with progressive level of detail. Bit-exact or nothing loads, and the failure surfaces in a log rather than on screen.

modules.name: Skeletons and animation
modules.why: 203 skeletons, 4,676 animations. Interpolation and track semantics have to match or everything moves wrongly.

modules.name: Terrain zones
modules.why: 7,561 zones, 1.49 GB, patch-based with tile banks. The densest format in the set.

modules.name: Instance groups
modules.why: Already inspected: name, shape, transform, repeated. 5,148 files, about 51 instances per cell.

modules.name: Collision data
modules.why: Feeds movement feel. A misread surface is felt rather than reported.

modules.name: Sheet format
modules.why: 34 packed sheets carry items, bricks, phrases, creatures and the skill tree. One wrong offset corrupts the whole content set.

modules.name: Primitives
modules.why: The populated world: spawns, NPCs, mission anchors. Licence of the data itself is unresolved.

modules.name: Particle systems
modules.why: 870 systems. Large surface, but a wrong one is visible immediately rather than silently.

modules.name: Graphics backend
modules.why: C# hands you no GPU abstraction, so this is written here. Choosing C# made this larger, and it is the single decision that could invalidate the plan.

modules.name: Terrain rendering
modules.why: Whether this holds the reference's draw distance and frame time is UNMEASURED. First risk to retire.

modules.name: Mesh and skinning
modules.why: Well-understood problem, large surface. Instancing decides whether crowds are affordable.

modules.name: Particle rendering
modules.why: Visual, self-evident when wrong.

modules.name: Sky, weather, day and night
modules.why: Strongly shapes how the world reads, but a mistake is cosmetic.

modules.name: Vegetation
modules.why: Density is a frame-time problem as much as a visual one.

modules.name: Deterministic capture
modules.why: Golden-frame testing depends on it being genuinely deterministic, not approximately.

modules.name: Cell grid and residency
modules.why: Naming and neighbourhood are simple; getting eviction wrong shows up as thrash.

modules.name: Streaming and budget
modules.why: Where the GC argument is won or lost. Must not allocate in the hot path, and 6.4 GB must stay off the managed heap.

modules.name: Collision and movement surface
modules.why: This IS game feel. Sliding along a wall and stepping over a lip decide whether movement feels right, and approximation is noticed immediately.

modules.name: Spatial index
modules.why: Shared by client and server. If the two disagree, players fall through the world.

modules.name: Wire schema compiler
modules.why: 474 properties and 335 impulses. A previous attempt assumed flat message ids and was wrong: addressing is a route through the tree.

modules.name: Bit-packed codec
modules.why: Bit widths come from sibling counts, so adding an entry re-encodes a branch. Silent corruption if wrong.

modules.name: Transport and sessions
modules.why: Transport choice is still open. QUIC would also open a browser path later.

modules.name: Property replication
modules.why: Interest scoping and per-client bandwidth priority decide whether a crowded scene feels right.

modules.name: Authoritative tick
modules.why: 10 Hz is a fidelity constraint: gameplay timing is expressed in ticks, so changing the rate rescales the whole game.

modules.name: Session and admission
modules.why: Well-understood territory, and the one place the existing web-API patterns apply in full.

modules.name: Entity registry
modules.why: Lifecycle and visibility. Allocation behaviour here is felt at every tick.

modules.name: Movement and modes
modules.why: Game feel, and the first thing a player judges. Fixed-point and collision have to agree exactly.

modules.name: Combat resolution
modules.why: The most fidelity-critical code in the project. Hit tables and effect ordering cannot be re-derived by reasoning, only matched against the oracle. Note: sabrina is the DEAD copy.

modules.name: Persistent effects
modules.why: One file per effect in the reference. Stacking and ordering are behaviour.

modules.name: Magic resolution
modules.why: Cast, resist, apply. Same exactness bar as combat.

modules.name: Craft and harvest
modules.why: Foraging is a signature system and its success curves are tuned, not derivable.

modules.name: Character, stats, progression
modules.why: character.cpp alone is 21,550 lines and character.h is included by 188 files. Large, coupled, and full of tuned numbers.

modules.name: Inventory and equipment
modules.why: Weight, bulk and slot rules are mechanical but numerous.

modules.name: Mob behaviour
modules.why: Aggro, groups and spawn cycles. Most behaviour is group-level, not per-creature, and it is judged by feel over time.

modules.name: Missions
modules.why: Large but mostly declarative once primitives are extracted.

modules.name: Guilds and factions
modules.why: Social systems: broad, shallow, low exactness bar.

modules.name: Outposts
modules.why: Self-contained gameplay with its own timing rules.

modules.name: Trade and economy
modules.why: Exploitable if wrong, so it needs care disproportionate to its size.

modules.name: Chat and server text
modules.why: Routing plus localisation of server-sent player text.

modules.name: Persistence
modules.why: The reference has a bespoke engine; a database replaces it. Migration correctness matters more than speed.

modules.name: Widget engine
modules.why: Layout, event routing, text and bindings. Large, but a well-understood problem.

modules.name: Property bindings
modules.why: The link between the property tree and the HUD. If a value is missing, the work is a contract change.

modules.name: HUD definitions
reference: interfaces_v3 (53,150 lines of markup and script)
modules.why: RE-AUTHORED window by window from observation, never converted: transforming their markup carries its expression. Paid across features rather than upfront.

modules.name: Action handlers
modules.why: The verbs the HUD invokes. Numerous and individually simple.

modules.name: Client core and session
modules.why: Boot, session, entity view, camera, prediction. Broad rather than deep.

modules.name: Visual entities and animation state
modules.why: Appearance composition and animation blending. Visible immediately when wrong.

modules.name: Sound
modules.why: Mature libraries exist; only the bank and sound-animation formats need decoding.

modules.name: Content extraction
modules.why: Fails quietly: a run that drops a category looks exactly like one that worked. Counts must reconcile on both sides.

modules.name: Rebrand mapping
modules.why: The brand seam. An unmapped term must fail extraction rather than travel downstream into a shipped build.

modules.name: Control plane
modules.why: Time control, state queries, snapshots, injection. Must be compiled out of release builds, not merely disabled.

modules.name: Scenario runner
modules.why: Turns a seed plus an input sequence into a complete, replayable bug report.

modules.name: MCP bridge
modules.why: The thin part. A transport over capability that already exists.
